doctype: For leaders & coaches · not a teacher handout
title: Year-One Rollout & Coaching Plan
subtitle: How we turn the 6–8 Math Toolbelt from a website into changed instruction. The plan is the lever; the toolbelt is the reference it points to.

sections.sources: Companion to the 6–8 Mathematics Toolbelt. Reflects a 6-judge feasibility review: lead with a mandated starter set, ship the coaching cycle as a co-deliverable, make equity moves default, and commit date-bound to rich-task Core Instruction.

blocks.text: The strategy on one page
We are moving a procedural-heavy 6–8 faculty toward reasoning and discourse by starting small, coaching hard, and building toward rich tasks.

blocks.title: The through-line that holds it together

blocks.text: The opener routines are **rehearsal for rich tasks**. Every move a teacher practices in a 12-minute Number Talk — eliciting strategies, revoicing, holding productive struggle, consolidating thinking — is exactly what a **three-act / rich task** demands at full scale. Fluency-first is not a detour from the destination; it is basic training for it. That is the story we tell teachers, and it is why the move into Core Instruction later is a natural next rep, not a leap.

items: **Where we start:** a short, discourse-rich *opener* (10–15 min) that rides on top of the adopted curriculum — not a competing program.
**Where we are going:** **rich tasks / three-act math** in Core Instruction (second semester / phase two), with a named readiness trigger.

**Honest cap (say this to leadership now):** year-one impact is real but bounded to ~15 minutes of the period; it will not move benchmark achievement until Core ships. Year one builds the muscle; the rich tasks move the needle.

blocks.text: The five non-negotiables (this is what makes or breaks it)

items: **A mandated starter set — not the full menu.** A discourse-novice faculty cannot choose from seven routines. We name the few, in order.
**The coaching cycle is the engine.** A reference website does not change practice; the model → co-plan → co-teach → debrief cycle does. PD days launch; coaching sustains.
**Equity moves are defaults, not options.** Turn-and-talk-before-share, posted sentence stems, and wait time are required structure in every routine.
**The opener replaces the warm-up — it is not added on top.** This protects the 12 minutes and the pacing guide.
**Protect productive struggle from the walkthrough.** Principals are briefed that productive noise and uncorrected errors are the goal, not a management problem.

blocks.text: The starter sequence
Talk Moves is the enabling *skill* and is taught first; then two routines, easy entry to coached anchor. Everything else is visibly marked “later.”

rows: **1. Foundation**
**Talk Moves** (start with wait time, then revoicing)
The prerequisite skill and the MLL/SWD access architecture. Without it, every routine collapses into teacher-and-three-hands. Teach it before any routine.
**2. First routine (gentle)**
**Same But Different**
Near-zero prep, lowest facilitation load, everyone can offer one “same” or “different.” Builds comparison and discourse without the live-recording demand.
**3. Coached anchor**
**Number Talks**
The highest-transfer routine to rich tasks — but the HARDEST to facilitate (live recording, suppressing the correction reflex). Introduce it WITH coaching, not as the cold start.
**Later (phase two)**
Number Strings, Quick Images & Splat, Would You Rather / Estimation, Error Analysis
Marked “next, once the first three are humming.” Added by purpose as the faculty gains discourse fluency.

rows: **Launch** [PD DAY 1 — DATE]

Kickoff: the vision, the through-line (openers = rehearsal for tasks), and the “When to Tell” guide (lead with this — it disarms “I’m not allowed to teach”). Teach **Talk Moves: wait time**. Norms & routine-launch management.
Whole-faculty PD day. Each teacher leaves with a 2-week wait-time commitment and one Same But Different ready to run.
Wait time becomes habit. Launch **Same But Different** 2–3×/week. Establish the opener as a *replacement* warm-up. Equity defaults in place (turn-and-talk, stems).
Coaching cycle round 1 on Same But Different (model → co-plan → co-teach → debrief). PLC: do-the-math-first.
Add revoicing + “who can add on.” Introduce **Number Talks** as the coached anchor. Expect it to feel hard — that’s why it’s coached, not cold.
Coaching cycle round 2 on Number Talks, with the “common novice failure modes” note. [PD DAY 2 — calibration].
Number Talks 2–3×/week running. Faculty fluent in the starter set. Begin adding a phase-two routine *by purpose* where teams are ready.
Coaching shifts from launch to refinement. PLCs self-running the protocol. Check the readiness signals (below).
**Semester 2** [DATE]
**Readiness trigger met → begin Core Instruction: rich tasks / three-act math.** Openers continue as the warm-up; the discourse muscle now scales to full tasks (5 Practices, vertical whiteboards).
[PD DAY 3 — rich tasks launch]. Coaching cycle pivots to task facilitation. This is where the leader’s heart — and the achievement movement — lives.

blocks.text: The coaching cycle — the engine
Run repeatedly through existing PLC and coaching time. One routine, one cycle, per team at a time.

items: **Model** — Coach (or a clip) demonstrates the routine in a real class; teachers watch for specific look-fors.
**Co-plan** — Coach + teacher plan the next routine together: choose the problem, anticipate strategies, pick one talk move.
**Co-teach / observe** — Teacher runs it; coach supports or observes against the “we want to see” list — non-evaluative.
**Debrief** — What did students do? What will we adjust? One concrete next step. Then cycle again.

blocks.text: Keep feedback observational, not evaluative — tie it to each tool’s “we want to see” list:

items: “I counted ___ seconds of wait time after your question. What did you notice about who answered?”
“You recorded ___ different strategies. Which student’s thinking do you wish you’d gotten to?”
“When [student] said the wrong answer, you ___. What were you deciding in that moment?”

blocks.text: The PLC protocol (repeatable agenda)

items: **Do the math first (10 min).** The team solves the routine/task themselves. This is the quiet content-knowledge lever — procedural teaching often reflects shaky teacher understanding.
**Anticipate student strategies (10 min).** Where will students go? What’s the likely misconception? (This is the seed of the 5 Practices.)
**Look at student work (15 min).** Bring artifacts / exit tickets from the last routine. What does the thinking show? *(Use the CFUs/exit tickets you already have.)*
**Rehearse one move (10 min).** Practice the talk move or recording aloud with each other.
**Plan the next routine (5 min).** Specific problem, specific move, specific day.

blocks.text: Classroom-management & routine-launch scaffolding
Routines die from management failure, not pedagogy failure. Equip teachers with these before they launch:

yes.title: Set teachers up with
items: Explicit norms: “talking is thinking; mistakes are useful; we build on each other”
Turn-and-talk as the pressure valve before any whole-group share
A move for “no one volunteers”: revoice a turn-and-talk you overheard, or cold-call a student you primed
A visible timer / 12-minute ceiling so it doesn’t eat the period
The rule: the opener *replaces* the old warm-up

no.title: Warn teachers about
items: Letting it run 25 minutes and abandoning the lesson
The blurter setting the pace — use think time + stems
The same four hands; track who hasn’t been heard (privately)
Filling silence themselves — wait time feels long and works
Turning it into graded practice

blocks.text: Equity defaults (non-negotiable in every routine)

items: **Turn-and-talk before public share**, **posted sentence stems**, and **wait time** — structural defaults, not optional callouts.

**Multilingual learners are not a monolith:** a newcomer / WIDA-1 student needs non-verbal entry (Quick Images, gesture, write/point) and is the reason that routine stays in the toolbelt; a long-term EL needs stems and revoicing.
**The second adult (co-teacher / ENL / para) amplifies, never replaces, thinking:** revoice, prime a student during turn-and-talk to be cold-called — do not do the math for them.
**Private participation self-monitor:** a once-a-week roster glance — “who haven’t I heard from?” Never a live job, never a collected log, never surveillance.

blocks.title: Principal / Admin brief — lift this verbatim

blocks.text: When you walk into a math opener this year, you should expect to see and hear things that look different from a quiet, orderly lecture. **That is the goal, not a problem:**

items: Productive noise — students talking to each other about math — is success.
Uncorrected wrong answers left on the board for discussion are intentional.
Silence after a question (wait time) is a skill, not a stall.
These walks are **for program health, not teacher evaluation.** Teachers are taking risks; do not penalize the risk-taking we asked for.

blocks.text: Readiness trigger: when to move to rich tasks (Core)
Don’t move on a date alone; move when the muscle is built. Signals the faculty is ready for three-act / rich tasks:

items: Starter routines run **2–3×/week in most rooms** without coaching present.
In a typical routine, **multiple student strategies** are shared and recorded, and students respond to each other (not just the teacher).
Teachers can **hold productive struggle** for a few minutes without rescuing.
PLCs run the do-the-math-first protocol on their own.

blocks.text: When those hold, launch **rich tasks / three-act math**: same discourse moves, now across a full lesson (anticipate → monitor → select → sequence → connect), at vertical whiteboards. This is the destination — and where benchmark movement becomes realistic.
Monitoring (leadership-side, light)
Keep the load off teachers. Know it’s working through:

items: **Coaching-cycle notes** (non-evaluative, aggregated) — where discourse is taking root district-wide, where to send more support.
**PLC artifacts** — teams bringing student work and planning routines.
**Student work samples** over time — are students showing more reasoning?
*(A leadership learning-walk look-for tool can come later — deliberately not built yet, and firewalled from teacher evaluation when it does.)*

blocks.text: What you already have working for you

rows: **Math coaches in buildings**
Run the coaching cycle — the engine of the whole plan.
**Scheduled PLC time**
The weekly home of the do-the-math-first protocol and student-work analysis.
**Dedicated PD days**
Launch & calibration points: [DAY 1] launch, [DAY 2] calibration, [DAY 3] rich-task launch.
**Adopted core curriculum**
The opener rides on top of it; the routines connect to the day’s content rather than competing with it.
**Existing CFUs / exit tickets**
Already teacher-owned — feed them into the PLC student-work step; yesterday’s exit ticket seeds today’s routine.
